title: Inference pacing audit & regression harness for sustained tokens/s and p95 tracking
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build and maintain an automated inference pacing audit and regression harness that measures sustained tokens-per-second and latency tail (p95/p99) across core models and representative sequence-length buckets. The harness will replay production-like token cadence, support KV cache warm/cold states, and produce time-series artifacts and histograms suitable for automated regression detection and Console dashboards. Deliverables: a reusable load generator, CI jobs and nightly runs, golden baselines in S3, alerting rules for regressions, and consumer-facing dashboard links.
acceptance_criteria: Load generator can run repeatable 30m probes that simulate production token cadence with configurable sequence-length distributions
Metrics captured: sustained tokens/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, median and tail token velocity, and histogram snapshots exported to Console and S3
Regression detector compares nightly results to baseline and raises alerts when TPS drops >6% or p95 increases >10% for a model-release, with a human-confirmation workflow
CI gate job runs on PRs touching runtime or model-serving code and fails on statistically significant regressions versus latest baseline
Documentation (design doc + runbook) and a stable dashboard with per-model baselines and drift history are published
technical_notes: Synthetic workload generator in Go with pluggable cadence profiles (poisson, bursty, steady); supports HTTP and internal RPC modes
Sequence length buckets: 8-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048; weighted sampling to match prod percentiles
KV cache states: cold, partially-warm (10% entries), fully-warm; warmup module seeds KV cache via representative prompts
Measurement window: sliding 60s token-rate with 5s resolution; aggregate 30m run to stabilize variance
Latency capture: per-token service latency + end-to-end response time; use hdrhistogram for p50/p95/p99 snapshots

Regression detection: baseline stored as time-series JSON in s3://redwood-bench/baselines/{model}/{release}; detection uses a two-tier rule: absolute threshold and normalized z-score over last 14 runs
Alerting integration: push regression events to Observability -> Console alerts and PagerDuty with link back to run artifacts
CI integration: lightweight smoke mode (5m, sampled traffic) for PRs and full mode (30m) for nightly runs; results artifactized as JSON for diffs
Golden baseline governance: baseline updates require manual review + signoff via GitHub PR including raw run artifacts and statistical summary
Cost control: runner supports max RPS and simultaneous sessions limits; runner will automatically backoff when observability reports backend overload
